images.title: An empty column breaks the number
images.purpose: Shows the core move of the zero placeholder breaker: leaving the 10s column empty makes 305 read as 35, while a 0 keeps it 305.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Before and after: two identical rows of three place columns, one with an empty column and one with a 0, each with the reading to its right.
images.exact_structure: Two rows, one above the other. Each row has three column boxes headed 100s, 10s, 1s in small grey (#6B7280). Top row: 3 and 5 in the 100s and 1s boxes, the 10s box empty with a vermilion (#D55E00) outline; to its right reads 35 in vermilion. Bottom row: 3, 0 and 5, the 0 tile in green (#009E73); to its right reads 305 in green. Exactly 6 boxes. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A 0 holds an empty place open; without it every digit to the left slips down a place.

image_decisions.why: The doer image shows the breaker's one contrast: an empty column versus a 0.
